# The Golden Oak · Book II, pp. 186–189
# Generated by the extractor — fix the extractor, not this file.
PAGE	186
P	On a clear day, sharp-eyed folk in Stonetop can spot the Golden Oak, gleaming at the horizon and dwarfing the trees around it.
P	According to the tales of the <b>Forest Folk</b> (page 150), a hero buried at the roots of the Oak can find their way back from beyond the <b>Last Door</b> (page 70). But no one from Stonetop has ever made it there and back.
H2	Questions
HR
Q	When was Stonetop's last expedition to the Golden Oak? Who were they trying to save?
Q	What other tales have you heard about the Oak? How much of them do you believe?
Q	Who would have to die for you to risk a journey to the Golden Oak?
H2	Getting there
HR
P	<b>Something interesting:</b> The Golden Oak doesn't quite exist in this world, at least not anymore. It can only be reached through Fae pathways, at great risk and personal cost.
P	When you <b><i>travel towards the Golden Oak</i></b> <b><i>in the mundane world</i></b>, you never reach it.
P	Even if you were to fly above the trees, it would remain always out of reach, its bearing shifting.
P	<b>Something useful:</b> To reach the Golden Oak, you must…
C	learn to walk the Fae paths (see <b>waystones</b>, page 478);
C	follow the Fae paths to a specific set of waystones, those closest to the Oak;
C	find a secret crossing and face its guardian, set there by the <b>Lady of</b> <b>Crows</b> herself (page 71); and
C	pay the Lady's due to make the crossing.
P	When you <b><i>pay the Lady's due</i></b>, choose 1 as a group:
B	Present a marker of the <b>Pale Hunter</b>'s favor (page 292), honestly earned
B	Each of you must make a sacrifice. Cross off a move you possess; it is gone and you cannot regain it. (Followers cross off a tag of the GM's choice instead.)
B	One of your number passes willingly through the Last Door, their body gone, never to be seen again.
P	When you <b><i>make the crossing</i></b>, you glimpse the Last Door and what lies beyond. Tell us what you see.
PAGE	187
H2	Setting the scene
HR
P	The Golden Oak itself is enormous, so big as to defy any sense of scale. The bark is pale and luminous, and the glittering canopy is distant as the sky.
Q	What detail do you notice that drives home the fact that everything here is huge and massive?
Q	What here tells you this is a place of primal, unchecked vitality?
Q	What do you notice about yourself, that tells you that something is making you more angry, savage, and violent?
H2	The savage curse
HR
P	This was once a hub of the <b>Green Lords</b>' civilization (page 210). When the <b>Fae</b> (page 94) rebelled and turned on their masters, they claimed it for themselves. The surviving Lords laid a curse of primal savagery on the place. The rebel Fae abandoned it and the <b>Lady of Crows</b> (page 71) sealed it away.
P	When you <b><i>are under the vast canopy of the</i></b> <b><i>Golden Oak</i></b>…
E	and you <b>Persuade using anything but</b> <b>violence or threats</b>, the best you can get is a 7-9.
E	and you <b>give in to the savagery in</b> <b>your heart</b>, regain 2d8 HP and become larger, more muscular, more bestial. Gain advantage when you roll STR and disadvantage when you roll WIS until you leave this place.
E	and you <b>fight with no mercy,</b> <b>hesitation, or remorse</b>, roll damage with advantage.
E	and you <b>seek to make something, heal</b> <b>someone, or repair something</b>, roll
P	+WIS: <b>on a 10+</b>, you can work as long as you keep focused on your task; <b>on a</b> <b>7-9</b>, you make some progress, but are easily distracted, frustrated, or enraged.

H2	Dangers
HR
P	Pick 1, or have someone roll the Die of Fate.
P	1d6 danger
HR
P	1 Enormous vermin—dog-sized, man-sized, horse-sized, or worse—each with some uncanny trait or mutation
P	2 Gargantuan beasts, crashing about you, disinterested and unconcerned
P	3 <b>Specters</b> (page 79) of betrayed Green Lords, like roving storms of hate
P	4 <b>Hollow Fae</b> (page 114), trapped here for ages, mad with soul-hunger
P	5 Pockets of dangerous old magic, ready to ensnare, rend, or mutate
P	6 An overwhelming urge to fight, to hurt, to kill. If they act on the impulse, they mark XP. If they resist, they are Defying Danger (probably with WIS).
H2	Discoveries
P	Pick 1, or have someone roll the Die of Fate.
P	1d6 discovery
P	1 A small pocket of safety: a cave, an old ruin, a hollow in a massive tree
P	2 The remains of a Green Lord or a rebel warrior, strangely well preserved
P	3 A dead beast: enormous, half-eaten, teeming with vermin
P	4 <b>Useful or valuable flora</b> (page 458), growing in preposterous proportions
P	5 A mad hermit, trapped here and lost in time (perhaps from a previous expedition?)
P	6 An artifact of... (roll d12)
P	1-7 The <b>Green Lords</b> (page 210)
P	8-11 The <b>Fae</b> (page 94)
P	12 The <b>Things Below</b> (page 412)

H2	Treasures of
HR
B	A living ◇ leaf from the Golden Oak can be made into a <b>Goldleaf</b> <b>Cloak</b> (page 517).
B	With proper tools and knowledge, the bark can be harvested to craft weapons or armor (2 armor, <i>warm</i>, <i>cumbersome</i>) that is hard as iron and bane to undead or things from beyond the Last Door.
B	A ◇◇ golden acorn, harvested in autumn, can be planted elsewhere to grow a <b>Golden Sapling</b> (see sidebar).
H2	Buried at the roots
HR
P	When you <b><i>bury a corpse at the roots of</i></b> <b><i>the Golden Oak</i></b>, close to the trunk, roll and add…
E	+1 if the corpse has not yet started to rot;
E	+1 if they died bravely in their prime; and
E	+1 if their name is still well-known.
P	<b>On a 10+</b>, they return from beyond the Last Door when the sun next rises, whole and healthy though likely shaken; <b>on a 7-9</b>, they do not yet rise, but maybe if you give it another night? <b>On a 6-</b>, they return, but something else comes with them, something dangerous and dark, something now tied to them in a deep and primal way.
TH	steading improvement
C	<b>GOLDEN SAPLING</b>
P	Requires all of the following, in order:
C	Retrieve an ◇◇ acorn from the boughs of the Golden Oak in late autumn
C	Plant the acorn in the fields near Stonetop, watering it with the lifeblood of a great virile beast, like an aurochs bull
C	Nurture and protect the sapling through 4 years of growth
P	When you <b><i>mark all the requirements</i></b>, add "Golden Sapling" to the Resources list and automatically mark the <b>Greater Harvest</b> improvement.
P	Henceforth, when the steading generates Surplus, even just 1, it generates +1 Surplus.
